title: A driving question the text can answer
statement: A lesson's driving question is open, never yes or no, answerable from the text alone, about what the text shows or how it shows it, and short.
detail: Texts dropped or pasted into the lesson engine's composer arrive without a lesson question. The engine drafts three, keeps in code those that end in a question mark, run to at most 26 words, open with no yes-or-no word and cite no line number, and asks the judge whether each can be answered from the passage alone and is worth a Grade 9 lesson of about an hour (`g9/transformer/src/question.js`, lines 12-34). The first one the judge confirms becomes the lesson question the blocks are written toward.
against: The judge's question joins two claims in one yes-or-no: "Can question_${i} be answered from passage alone, and is it worth a Grade 9 lesson of about an hour?" (`g9/transformer/src/question.js`, line 34). The prompt asks for at most 22 words while code allows 26 (lines 23 and 12), and the first confirmed question is kept, not the best one: "question = qs.find((_, i) => results[i]?.verdict === "holds") ?? null;" (line 35).

evidence.quote: Each is open (never yes or no), answerable from the text alone, about what the text shows or how it shows it, at most 22 words, ending in "?".
The writer drafts three; code keeps … the open, well-formed ones; the judge keeps the first it finds answerable from the text alone and worth a lesson
